content.stem:
The points \(A(1, 2)\) and \(B(4, 3)\) are plotted on the grid.

(i) \(A\) and \(B\) are reflected in the x-axis to \(A'\) and \(B'\) respectively. Write down the coordinates of \(A'\) and \(B'\).

(ii) Name the figure \(ABB'A'\) and find its area.

diagrams.alt: A coordinate grid with the x-axis from -1 to 6 and the y-axis from -4 to 4, one unit per square. Point A is plotted at (1, 2) and point B at (4, 3), both above the x-axis.
diagrams.solutionAlt: A′ appears at (1, −2) joined to A by a dashed vertical line, then B′ appears at (4, −3) joined to B by a dashed vertical line, and finally the four-sided figure ABB′A′ (a trapezium) is shaded.

hints: When a point is reflected in the x-axis, which coordinate stays the same and which changes sign?
Look at the sides \(AA'\) and \(BB'\): how are they placed relative to each other?

solution.modelAnswer:
(i) Reflection in the x-axis: \((x, y) \to (x, -y)\), so \(A'(1, -2)\) and \(B'(4, -3)\).

(ii) \(AA'\) and \(BB'\) are both vertical, so \(AA' \parallel BB'\) and \(ABB'A'\) is a trapezium. \(AA' = 4\), \(BB' = 6\) and the distance between them is \(4 - 1 = 3\). Area \(= \tfrac{1}{2}(4 + 6) \times 3 = 15\) sq. units.
solution.finalAnswer: \(A'(1, -2)\), \(B'(4, -3)\); \(ABB'A'\) is a trapezium (isosceles trapezium) of area 15 sq. units.

steps.title: Rule for reflection in the x-axis
steps.explanation: Reflecting in the x-axis keeps the x-coordinate and changes the sign of the y-coordinate. The image is the same distance below the axis as the point is above it.

steps.title: Image of A
steps.explanation: \(A\) is 2 units above the x-axis, so \(A'\) is 2 units below it, directly underneath.

steps.title: Image of B
steps.explanation: \(B\) is 3 units above the x-axis, so \(B'\) is 3 units below it.

steps.title: Name the figure
steps.explanation: Both \(AA'\) and \(BB'\) are perpendicular to the x-axis, so they are parallel. \(AB\) and \(A'B'\) are not parallel (they slope in opposite directions), so \(ABB'A'\) is a trapezium. It is symmetric about the x-axis, so it is an isosceles trapezium.
steps.reason: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is a trapezium.

steps.title: Area of the trapezium
steps.explanation: \(AA' = 2 - (-2) = 4\) and \(BB' = 3 - (-3) = 6\). The perpendicular distance between the parallel sides is the difference of their x-coordinates, \(4 - 1 = 3\).
steps.rule: Area of a trapezium \(= \tfrac{1}{2} \times (\text{sum of parallel sides}) \times \text{height}\)

commonMistakes: Changing the sign of the x-coordinate instead, i.e. reflecting in the y-axis: writing \(A'(-1, 2)\).
Taking the height of the trapezium as 4 or 6 (a parallel side) instead of the horizontal distance 3 between the parallel sides.
Calling the figure a parallelogram or a rectangle; \(AB\) and \(A'B'\) are not parallel.

alternativeMethods.title: Coordinate (shoelace) formula
alternativeMethods.description: With vertices \(A(1, 2), B(4, 3), B'(4, -3), A'(1, -2)\) taken in order, the area formula \(\tfrac{1}{2}\left|\sum (x_i y_{i+1} - x_{i+1} y_i)\right|\) also gives 15 sq. units.

alternativeMethods.title: Counting squares
alternativeMethods.description: On graph paper the trapezium can be split into a \(3 \times 4\) rectangle (area 12) and two right triangles each of area \(\tfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 1 = 1.5\), giving \(12 + 3 = 15\).

acceptedAlternatives: Points correctly plotted and labelled on the graph with coordinates stated
criteria.partialCreditRules: Both images must be correct for this mark.

criteria.description: Names the figure as a trapezium
criteria.expectedEvidence: ABB'A' is a trapezium (isosceles trapezium accepted), ideally noting AA' ∥ BB'
Parallel sides 4 and 6 and height 3 substituted into ½(a + b)h, or an equivalent correct method
acceptedAlternatives: Splitting into a rectangle and triangles
criteria.partialCreditRules: Follow-through: award if the method is correct using the student's own (wrong) image coordinates, provided the figure is still a trapezium.

questions.authorNotes: Diagram is to scale on a 1-unit grid. The figure is an isosceles trapezium (symmetric about the x-axis); 'trapezium' alone earns the naming mark. Numeric answer key refers to the area in part (ii).

content.stem: The point \((-3, 5)\) is reflected in the line \(y = 2\). The coordinates of its image are:

hints: The line \(y = 2\) is horizontal, so the x-coordinate does not change. How far is the point above the line?

solution.modelAnswer: The point is \(5 - 2 = 3\) units above the line \(y = 2\), so its image is 3 units below it: \(y = 2 - 3 = -1\). The x-coordinate is unchanged. Image \((-3, -1)\), option (b).

steps.title: Distance from the mirror line
steps.explanation: The line \(y = 2\) is horizontal. The point \((-3, 5)\) is 3 units above it.
steps.reason: In a reflection, the image is the same perpendicular distance from the mirror line, on the other side.

steps.title: Find the image
steps.explanation: Go 3 units below the line. The x-coordinate stays \(-3\) because the mirror line is horizontal. This is option (b).

commonMistakes: Option (a): reflecting in the x-axis instead of the line \(y = 2\).
Option (c): reflecting in the line \(x = 2\), which changes the x-coordinate instead.
Option (d): using \(y' = b - y = 2 - 5\) instead of \(y' = 2b - y\).
